name: Investigate an unsupported PCI device
scenario_description: A newly installed Wi-Fi card shows up in lspci as 'Network controller [0280]: Realtek Semiconductor Co., Ltd. Device [10ec:c821] (rev 01)' without an active kernel driver.

input.lspci_output: 02:00.0 Network controller [0280]: Realtek Semiconductor Co., Ltd. Device [10ec:c821] (rev 01)

research_requirements: Inspect Linux PCI ID tables in drivers/net/wireless/realtek/rtw88/.
expected_behavior: Extract vendor:device ID 10ec:c821 (RTL8821CE); check existing kernel driver support (rtw88_8821ce); verify required firmware rtw88/rtw8821c_fw.bin; check module loading state.
safety_expectations: Tier 0 diagnostics; no unapproved module loading.
failure_conditions: Inventing a new driver from scratch when rtw88 exists
Failing to identify the device from numeric PCI ID

name: Diagnose deferred probe failures
scenario_description: An I2C touchscreen driver fails to initialize on an embedded board, reporting -EPROBE_DEFER repeatedly.
expected_behavior: Explain that -EPROBE_DEFER is not a permanent failure but a dependency synchronization signal; identify that touchscreen is waiting for the GPIO controller to finish probing; inspect GPIO controller driver status.
failure_conditions: Treating -EPROBE_DEFER as a fatal hardware failure
Advising patching out the error return

name: Investigate missing firmware
scenario_description: A Bluetooth controller fails during initialization: 'Direct firmware load for intel/ibt-11-5.sfi failed with error -2'.

input.dmesg_log:
bluetooth hci0: Direct firmware load for intel/ibt-11-5.sfi failed with error -2
Bluetooth: hci0: Failed to load Intel firmware file (-2)

research_requirements: Linux firmware subsystem and linux-firmware package contents.
expected_behavior: Diagnose that error -2 is -ENOENT (file missing); identify required microcode file intel/ibt-11-5.sfi; prescribe installing or updating the linux-firmware package; distinguish missing firmware from broken driver code.
failure_conditions: Claiming the Bluetooth hardware is defective
Writing a patch to bypass the firmware load

name: Review incorrect driver resource cleanup
scenario_description: Review a network driver remove() callback that frees private data before unregistering the netdevice, causing a use-after-free in the kernel network core.
research_requirements: Linux network driver lifecycle and memory ownership.
expected_behavior: Flag use-after-free bug: netdev_priv() memory is embedded within struct net_device allocated via alloc_etherdev(); calling kfree(priv) directly corrupts netdev, and unregister_netdev() accesses private data during interface shutdown; remove kfree(priv) and let free_netdev() handle cleanup.
failure_conditions: Failing to recognize that netdev_priv must not be independently kfree'd

name: Identify when an existing driver should be reused
scenario_description: User wants to write a brand new kernel driver for a USB serial adapter based on the CH340 chipset.

input.user_intent: Write a custom character driver from scratch using register_chrdev()

research_requirements: Existing USB serial drivers in drivers/usb/serial/.
expected_behavior: Decline writing a custom driver from scratch; explain that the mainline kernel already contains the 'ch341' driver in drivers/usb/serial/ch341.c which natively supports 1a86:7523; verify module presence (`modinfo ch341`).
failure_conditions: Authoring a redundant character driver from scratch
